tagline.text: A Benguet highland town where flower fields and vegetable farms spread out above the clouds

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–March (flowers, cherry blossoms, cool dry season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000–2,500 per person (a day trip from Baguio)

items.credit: Anne Zanne / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: A Benguet highland town about two hours north of Baguio along the Halsema Highway. Vegetable farms and flower plantations step down mountain slopes above 2,000m elevation, and in winter, frost, cherry blossoms, and a sea of clouds greet visitors.
Atok is a mountain town in the middle of Benguet province, about
50km
from Baguio. The entire town sits across steep terrain at roughly

elevation, and the Halsema Highway connecting Baguio and Bontoc runs along its ridgeline. Long home to the Kankanaey and Ibaloi peoples, it's now one of the Philippines' leading "vegetable baskets," known for highland crops like cabbage, potatoes, and carrots, as well as carnation farming.
Atok holds the former highest point of the Halsema Highway, at about

elevation, once the highest point on any Philippine national road. It held the title of "highest road in the Philippines" for years, until a road in Tinoc, Ifugao province, was confirmed to be higher in
. The trail up Mount Timbac (about
elevation), Luzon's third-highest peak, also starts in this area.
Atok is one of the coldest places in the Philippines. Dawn temperatures in
December–February
drop to around

, and in especially cold years, frost on the vegetable farms even makes the news. It's a worry for farmers, but for travelers it's a rare sight in a tropical country, drawing many visitors during this season.

More recently, the Northern Blossom flower farm and a cherry blossom park have become known, boosting Atok's popularity as a "highland drive" day trip from Baguio. There are no grand tourist facilities, but the fields and flowers spread across mountainsides above the clouds, along with the cool air, give it an exotic feel. It suits travelers wanting to add a day to a Baguio trip, and couples or families who enjoy photography.

A roughly 2-hectare flower farm on the slopes of Sayangan village, filled with ornamental rose cabbage, which grows into rose-like shapes, along with temperate flowers like sunflowers, snapdragons, and hydrangeas. On clear days, Mount Timbac and a sea of clouds unfold beyond the flower fields.
A park created in
by planting Japanese cherry trees, which bloom pink and white each year around
late January–March
. Bloom timing varies year to year, so check local updates before you go.
The site of a marker stone and viewpoint announcing an elevation of 7,400 feet (about 2,255m). It's a good spot to take a photo and rest with a warm cup of Benguet coffee from the nearby stall.

Vegetable farms cut like steps almost to the mountaintops are Atok's most common yet striking sight. Pull over almost anywhere along the Halsema Highway and you'll look down on fields of green and brown interspersed with plastic greenhouses.

blocks.title: An easy hike up Mount Timbac

children.text: One of Luzon's three highest peaks, but from the trailhead on the Halsema Highway side, it's only about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
to the summit. On the opposite slope lie Kabayan's Timbac mummy caves.

blocks.title: Watch the dawn sea of clouds and frost

children.text: A sea of clouds commonly fills the valley on winter mornings, and on cold days, white frost settles on the fields.
6–8 AM
is the best window.

The Sayangan public market and roadside stalls sell freshly picked vegetables, strawberries, and flower bouquets cheaper than in Baguio. Stopping to shop on the way back is one of the trip's pleasures.

Mount Timbac requires visitor registration at the trailhead and using a local guide as standard practice. The pre-dawn hike is very cold, so be sure to pack warm clothing.
Baguio-bound buses such as Victory Liner and Genesis leave frequently from Cubao, Pasay, and elsewhere in Manila. It takes about
4–6 hours
and the fare is about
depending on class. To see Atok's dawn scenery, it's best to stay in Baguio the night before.
Buses toward Sagada, Bontoc, or Buguias, or vans bound for Atok, from around the Dangwa terminal or the Slaughterhouse terminal in Baguio, pass through Atok along the Halsema Highway. It takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours 30 minutes
, for a fare of around

Tell the driver in advance where you want to get off — "Northern Blossom," "Sayangan," or "Highest Point," for example. For the return trip, flag down a Baguio-bound vehicle along the road, though these become scarce later in the afternoon.
At the Dangwa Terminal (behind Baguio Center Mall), vehicles toward Atok run from around
5 AM
to around
6 PM
. Northern Blossom is beside the road in Sayangan village, so you get off and walk in.
To cover several spots before dawn, chartering a vehicle with a driver or a taxi in Baguio is the most convenient option. It runs about
round trip (one vehicle, 4–5 people), and Baguio travel agencies also offer day tours to Atok.
The Halsema Highway is a mountain road with continuous curves, cliff edges, and frequent fog. If you're driving yourself, go slowly and stick to daytime hours.
The nearest international airport is Clark International Airport (CRK); from there, take a bus to Baguio, about
3–4 hours
, then transfer to an Atok-bound vehicle.
The best season for an Atok trip is
December–March
. This period has little rain and clear skies, good for viewing the sea of clouds and sunrise, and the flower farms are also at their most vivid in
February–March
. Cherry blossoms generally peak around
late January–February
, though timing varies considerably year to year. In exchange, dawn temperatures drop to
, so a padded jacket or heavy coat is needed.
April–May
is pleasant even at midday, around
, but the chances of seeing a sea of clouds drop. The
June–October

rainy season brings thick fog and frequent rain, and when a typhoon hits, landslides and rockfalls can block sections of the Halsema Highway. If you're visiting during the rainy season, finish your itinerary in the morning and head back down promptly in the afternoon.

Atok has almost no proper hotels, so most visitors stay in Baguio and come as a day trip. Baguio has plenty of accommodation at about
a night. If you want to catch the Mount Timbac sunrise or the dawn sea of clouds, homestays, lodges, and campsites along the Halsema Highway toward Atok and Buguias are available at about
per person. Many lack heating, so bring warm clothes.

Food here revolves around vegetables, as befits a highland town. Roadside restaurants serve stir-fries and soups made with freshly picked cabbage, broccoli, and potatoes, along with Cordillera-style soups featuring etag, salted and smoked pork. On cold mornings, Benguet Arabica coffee with a warm bowl of soup hits the spot, and during strawberry season (roughly December–April), roadside strawberries and strawberry taho are also worth trying.
Early morning is best for the flower farms and the sea of clouds. Leave Baguio around
5 AM
to catch the scenery where sunlight and mist meet.
Dawn temperatures in December–February drop into the single digits Celsius. Bring a padded jacket, hat, and gloves, and dress in layers.
Northern Blossom tickets often come with a set visiting window. Plan your photos before you go in.
Northern Blossom
closes on Sundays
and can be entered only Monday to Saturday,
and
1 PM–4:30 PM
. Admission is
for adults (
for seniors and persons with disabilities) and includes Benguet coffee and bread. It's best to arrive at opening time on an uncrowded Monday to Thursday.
The flower and vegetable fields are farmers' livelihoods. Stick to the marked paths, and don't pick flowers or walk into the fields.
Cherry blossom timing and how the park operates change year to year. Check Atok tourism information or the latest notices before you set out.
The road curves continuously, so bring motion-sickness medicine and don't set out on an empty stomach.
ATMs are scarce along the road. Get cash for admission, transport, and shopping in Baguio beforehand.
This route connects well with the Kabayan Mummy Caves and Sagada. If you're planning a Cordillera loop, consider making Atok a stop along the way.

The Halsema Highway is a mountain road with heavy fog and many cliff edges. Landslides often block it after the rainy season and typhoons, so check road conditions before you set out, and don't stand at the road's edge to take photos.
Above 2,000m elevation, it can suddenly turn cold or start raining. Bring waterproof outerwear.
Parking carelessly on the shoulder blocks vegetable trucks and creates a hazard. Park at a viewpoint or a designated spot.
Some fields are sprayed with pesticides. Don't pick or touch the crops.
Always hike Mount Timbac before dawn with a guide, and bring a headlamp and warm gear.
Admission and environmental fees change often. Check the latest notice and get a receipt.
